speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have a two-day history of fever and altered mental status; to begin our evaluation, have you had any recent travel, insect bites, or contact with sick animals?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, are you experiencing any muscle rigidity, "lead-pipe" stiffness, or drooling? Also, please confirm if you have experienced any recent insect bites or travel to rural areas.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)

The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is highly suggestive of NMS. I am requesting a Creatine Kinase (CK) level and a urine myoglobin test to confirm the diagnosis and rule out rhabdomyolysis. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase; REQUEST TEST: Urine_Myoglobin
